slides.title: Launching Dispatch Copilot

paragraphs.text: Launching Dispatch Copilot
Should we launch in Q2 2027, and how should we package and price it?
Brightwork
CEO and executive team
Discussion document; synthetic benchmark data from the briefing pack

slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and with what package and price, to lift NRR from 101% to 105% by 2028 while keeping gross margin at 75% or more?
Does Copilot create value, and how many customers will pay $149 for it?
How much business does Routewise's AI cost us, and what does it mean for packaging?
Which package and price lift NRR to 105% and keep gross margin at 75% or more?
Is Copilot worth delaying the technician mobile app rewrite by two quarters?
How should we launch Pro, and what will tell us it is working?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO Maya Okafor and the executive team, at January 2027 planning

Net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028; Company gross margin at or above 75%; A credible answer to Routewise's AI in contested deals; The mobile app rewrite delayed by no more than two quarters
January 2027 planning
Building or switching the AI model; Engineering headcount above 60; The price of the Core plan

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of new ARR
Customers value Copilot, but a $149 add-on would bring about $2.5M of new ARR, not $8M
–	Beta productivity rose 9 percentage points more than in matched accounts
–	Only 14% bought at $149, against 46% 'likely' in the survey
Routewise has put AI in its plan, but matching it protects at most about $0.6M of new ARR a year
–	Win rate against Routewise fell from 44% to 37%, alongside a 20% discount
A Pro plan at $12 more per seat lifts NRR past 105% in its migration year and keeps margin above 75%
–	Pro needs about 26% of accounts to move; 33% moved to the 2023 tier
–	Copilot free in Core would cut gross margin to about 71.9%
Launching first is worth the two-quarter mobile delay, narrowly: mobile is the bigger churn problem
–	Mobile reliability is cited in 4.5 times as many churn cases as AI
–	The delay risks up to $1.1M of ARR; waiting defers $1.44M of Pro revenue
Launch Pro in Q2 2027 with a usage allowance, restart mobile in Q3 and review at six months
–	Cap use at about 444 requests per seat a month, with paid overage
